test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 03 May 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Three metal rods of length 77 cm, 110 cm and 121 cm are to be cut into parts of equal length. Each part must be as long as possible. What is the maximum number of pieces that can be cut?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To get pieces as long as possible, length of each piece must be HCF(77, 110, 121).

HCF(77, 110, 121) = 11 cm.

Total pieces = (Length 1 ÷ HCF) + (Length 2 ÷ HCF) + (Length 3 ÷ HCF)

Total pieces = (77 ÷ 11) + (110 ÷ 11) + (121 ÷ 11)

Total pieces = 7 + 10 + 11 = 28.

**∴ The correct option is B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Lengths of metal rods = 77 cm, 110 cm, 121 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Maximum length of each part = HCF of rod lengths.

Total number of pieces = (Total length of all rods) ÷ (Length of one part).

 
 77 cm (7 × 11 cm)
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 110 cm (10 × 11 cm)
 
• 
 
 
 121 cm (11 × 11 cm)
 
• 

 Each segment length = HCF(77, 110, 121) = 11 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factors of 77 = 7 × 11

⇒ Prime factors of 110 = 2 × 5 × 11

⇒ Prime factors of 121 = 11 × 11

⇒ HCF (77, 110, 121) = 11 cm

⇒ Max length of each part = 11 cm

⇒ Number of pieces from Rod 1 = 77 ÷ 11 = 7

⇒ Number of pieces from Rod 2 = 110 ÷ 11 = 10

⇒ Number of pieces from Rod 3 = 121 ÷ 11 = 11

⇒ Total maximum pieces = 7 + 10 + 11 = 28

**∴ The correct option is B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

It is the greatest number that divides each of the given numbers exactly without leaving any remainder.

Cutting Problems

When objects of different lengths are cut into equal pieces of maximum possible length, that length is always the HCF of the original lengths.

Number of Pieces Formula

Total Pieces = (Σ Lengths) ÷ HCF. Here, (77 + 110 + 121) ÷ 11 = 308 ÷ 11 = 28.</p
